solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Torture device, hence squad must bring in doctor

indicators.note: the pair of words must take another piece inside them, here early in the first

parts.note: hence means thus, therefore
MB, Bachelor of Medicine, is a doctor's qualification
a squad is a crew or team

explanation.surface: A torturer's logic: the squad has to bring a doctor along to the interrogation.
explanation.walkthrough: The doctor's letters sit inside the first word of the charade, not between the two words.
explanation.definitionFit: A screw device for crushing the digits, historically used to extract confessions.

clue.text: Haunt? Go and haunt wildly

indicators.note: wildly says the letters of these two words are thrown into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A spooky instruction: go off and haunt with abandon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Haunt' appears twice: the first is the definition (a place one frequents), the second is fodder; 'and' just joins.
explanation.definitionFit: A haunt is a place someone visits often, a favourite spot to spend time.

clue.text: Crazy to consume English alcoholic drink

indicators.note: to consume is to take in, so the first word swallows the second

parts.note: crazy means mad

explanation.surface: Someone thinks it mad to down an English booze.
explanation.definitionFit: Mead is a fermented honey beverage, an old alcoholic tipple.

clue.text: Saying nothing is kept up over period of religious observance

indicators.note: in a down clue, over places the first piece above the next
in a down clue, kept up means the word is read upwards, so backwards

parts.note: taken as written
Lent is the forty days of fasting before Easter

explanation.surface: Silence is maintained throughout a holy season of fasting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'kept up' turns IS into SI in this down clue; 'over' puts it above LENT.
explanation.definitionFit: Mute or quiet: someone keeping quiet is not speaking.

clue.text: Leaving job, being shy

definitions.meaning: stepping down from work at the end of a career

explanation.surface: A timid person quits work.
explanation.definitionFit: One sense is giving up work for good; the other describes a modest, reserved nature.

clue.text: Loss at sea with not taking care? Not half

indicators.note: not half means one half of the word is left off, here its second half

parts.note: reckless means careless, heedless

explanation.surface: A careless captain loses a ship, and the question is whether the blame is only partial.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not half' drops LESS from RECKLESS, leaving RECK; 'Not half' also reads as slang for 'very much'.
explanation.definitionFit: A shipwreck is the loss of a vessel at sea.

clue.text: Conventional source of water and power involving river

parts.note: a water main is a pipe supplying water

indicators.note: involving means taking in, so one piece is placed inside the other

parts.note: steam is a source of power

explanation.surface: A utility company provides standard water and energy, drawing on a river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'source of water and power' reads as one phrase (mains), but it splits: the water piece, then 'power' alone.
explanation.definitionFit: Mainstream thinking is the ordinary, orthodox view held by most people.

clue.text: Arcade game supplying a great time after a lot of beer

indicators.note: after puts the first-named piece later, behind the second-named piece

parts.note: a pin is a small cask holding four and a half gallons of beer
having a ball means having a great time

explanation.surface: An amusement arcade machine gives plenty of fun once the beer has flowed.
explanation.walkthrough: A pin is an old British cask size, half a firkin.
explanation.definitionFit: A coin-operated machine where a ball is flipped around a sloping table is a classic arcade amusement.

clue.text: Simple changes in historic document with multiple texts

indicators.note: in places the shuffled letters inside the other word

parts.note: historic means past, belonging to bygone times

indicators.note: changes says the letters of the word are altered into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Minor edits made to an old manuscript that has been written over several times.
explanation.walkthrough: 'historic document' looks like the definition, but 'historic' is wordplay; the definition is the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: A manuscript scraped and reused, with earlier writing still faintly visible beneath later writing.

clue.text: Letter and article presented with show of gratitude

parts.note: the is the definite article
ta is British informal for thank you

explanation.surface: A letter and a newspaper article arrive along with a thank-you.
explanation.walkthrough: TA is everyday British slang for thanks.
explanation.definitionFit: Theta is the eighth character of the Greek alphabet.

clue.text: Returned funds for circuit

indicators.note: returned means sent back, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: a pool is a shared fund of money

explanation.surface: Money handed back for a racing track or electrical circuit.
explanation.definitionFit: A loop is a closed path or round course, like a lap.

clue.text: Continuing sunny at heart, with no money invested

indicators.note: invested means put in, as money is put into something, so one piece goes inside
at heart takes the middle letters of the word, dropping its ends

parts.note: broke means penniless

explanation.surface: Staying cheerful at heart despite having nothing to invest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at heart' keeps all of sunny but its outer letters, three in all, not just the single central one.
explanation.definitionFit: An unbroken run is one that carries on without interruption.

clue.text: Hat, gloomy in colour — the reverse of golden

parts.note: sombre means dark and dull in colour

indicators.note: the reverse of means the word is written backwards

parts.note: or is the heraldic word for gold

explanation.surface: A hat whose drab colour is the opposite of golden.
explanation.definitionFit: A wide-brimmed Mexican hat.

clue.text: Approach satisfied head of department initially

parts.note: met as in met a requirement, satisfied it

indicators.note: initially takes the first letter of each of the three words

explanation.surface: An approach that pleased the head of department from the start.
explanation.definitionFit: A way of doing something, a technique or procedure.

clue.text: King, at the end of the day, is a chess piece

parts.note: K is the chess abbreviation for king

parts.words: at the end of the day
parts.note: night comes when the day ends

explanation.surface: A cliché: ultimately the king is just another chess piece.
explanation.walkthrough: 'At the end of the day' reads as a cliché meaning 'ultimately' but is taken literally.
explanation.definitionFit: The horse-shaped piece in chess that moves in an L shape.

clue.text: Real information leading a Parisienne to embrace one

indicators.note: leading puts the first piece in front of the next one

parts.note: gen is British slang for information

indicators.note: to embrace is to hug, so one piece wraps round another

parts.note: une is the French feminine for a
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Genuine intelligence prompting a Paris woman to hug someone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a Parisienne' is the feminine French word for 'a', not a woman from Paris.
explanation.definitionFit: Authentic, not fake: something real is the true article.

clue.text: Demon securing King's mate

indicators.note: securing means holding fast, so the first word encloses the second

parts.note: a fiend is a demon
R, for Rex, stands for king

explanation.surface: A devil captures the king's companion, perhaps in chess.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mate' suggests checkmate after 'King', but it means a pal.
explanation.definitionFit: A mate is a pal or companion.

clue.text: Part of swordsman's kit shows evidence of damage by poet

parts.note: a scab forms where skin has been damaged
a bard is a poet

explanation.surface: A swordsman's gear bears marks of damage caused by a poet.
explanation.definitionFit: The sheath in which a sword is carried, part of a swordsman's equipment.

clue.text: Daughter engaged in excuse, mostly dreamt up on the spot

indicators.note: engaged in means taking part inside, so the letter goes within the other piece
mostly means most but not all, so the final letter is dropped

parts.note: an alibi is an excuse

explanation.surface: A daughter makes up an excuse on the spur of the moment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mostly' cuts ALIBI to ALIB; 'engaged in' puts D inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Improvised: something made up spontaneously without preparation.

clue.text: Queen is appropriate in disregarding Times

indicators.note: disregarding means ignoring, so that letter is removed

parts.note: to annex is to appropriate, take over
X is the multiplication sign, read as times

explanation.surface: A monarch's suitability is judged without regard to the newspaper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Times' looks like the newspaper but is the multiplication sign.
explanation.definitionFit: Anne was an English monarch, reigning 1702 to 1714.

clue.text: Lavish religious instruction supplied by church

parts.note: RI is the abbreviation for religious instruction, a British school subject

explanation.surface: Generous teaching of faith provided by a church.
explanation.definitionFit: Opulent, sumptuous: both describe abundance.

clue.text: Work out alone — very into that

indicators.note: into means going inside, so the letter is placed within the word

parts.note: sole means single, alone

explanation.surface: Figure something out by yourself, getting deeply into it.
explanation.definitionFit: To find the answer to a problem by reasoning.

clue.text: Choosing the best extract from novel — it is marvellous

indicators.note: extract from says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A literary critic quotes a passage from a book while praising it lavishly.
explanation.definitionFit: Favouring a select few, the cream, over everyone else.

clue.text: Minor way these will get represented in newspaper

parts.note: a B road is a minor British road, below an A road

indicators.note: represented reads as re-presented, set out again in another order

explanation.surface: These minor roads will be shown in the paper.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain, B roads are minor roads; 'will get represented' shuffles THESE into SHEET.
explanation.definitionFit: A large-format newspaper, traditionally the serious kind.
